## Introduction

This analysis explores how physical characteristics differ across three
penguin species in the Palmer Penguins dataset. I focus on body mass and
flipper length to compare the species and look for patterns in their
measurements.

Data source: [Palmer Penguins](https://allisonhorst.github.io/palmerpenguins/),
Palmer Station Antarctica LTER.


## Exploring the data

I first load the dataset and inspect its structure

```{python}
#| warning: false
#| 
import pandas as pd
from palmerpenguins import load_penguins

penguins_data = load_penguins()

penguins_data.head(10)
```

```{python}
penguins_data.shape
penguins_data.columns
```

The dataset contains individual penguin observations and several physical
measurements, including body mass and flipper length.

```{python}
species_summary = (
    penguins_data.groupby("species").agg(average_body_mass=("body_mass_g", "mean"),
        average_flipper_length=("flipper_length_mm", "mean")
    )
    .round(1)
)

species_summary
```


The summary makes it possible to compare the typical physical measurements
of each species rather than individual penguins.

## Visualizing body mass

```{python}
#| label: fig-penguin-mass
#| fig-cap: "Average body mass of Palmer penguins by species."

species_summary["average_body_mass"].plot(
    kind="bar",
    ylabel="Average body mass (g)",
    xlabel="Species"
)
```


The figure shows that Gentoo penguins have the highest average body mass,
while Adelie penguins have the lowest average body mass among the three
species.

## Conclusion

The analysis shows clear physical differences between the three penguin
species. Gentoo penguins are heavier on average and also have longer
flippers, suggesting that body size varies substantially by species in
this dataset.
